endorsements.quote: Although these impacts may be invisible to health care institutions that deploy AI systems, it is worth interrogating how assessments of the potential benefits of AI to medical practice are weighed against these and other indirect harms to populations that may already be experiencing disproportionate health risks.
As AMCs and other health systems consider investments in AI projects, they should similarly consider appropriate resourcing and funding for addressing ethics and safety concerns.
As AMCs consider broader implementation of AI, assessments of whether these endeavors are beneficial to the patients and communities they serve will be paramount.

unlisted_practices: Include communities historically marginalized in health care in assessments of AI and treat their input as central to the technological design of health care AI.
Establish patient and community advisory boards to advise institutional leadership on health care AI initiatives and co-design AI systems with patients.
Support translational ethics research to prospectively identify harms and develop practical tools for applying ethical principles to health care AI.
Expand AI ethics education for clinicians, scientists, and trainees through courses, journal clubs, and seminars.
Report on and share institutional approaches to safe and ethical health care AI, whether successes or failures, and consider pooling resources across institutions.
Establish transparency about values and priorities when designing and implementing AI technologies.
Obtain patient disclosure and authorization when patient data is acquired and shared to develop AI technologies.
Obtain patient consent before integrating AI technologies into their care or analyzing their health record data.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework paper providing guidance and recommendations for academic medical centers on safe and ethical implementation and oversight of health care AI.
